precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 9:9
precepts.why:
“It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” A help meet is someone to help him through his daily chores and through living, something to his liking, something for him. God first brought every beast and fowl to Adam, and Adam named them all, because he was over them. Then it says, “but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.” Nothing yet was just for him.

So “the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam”, took one of his ribs, “made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” This is the Most High doing this for his son, and that is a gift. The gift still remains today for every man. That is why we call her your rib: there is a woman made just for you, because it is not good for man to be alone.

Solomon says what to do with that gift: “Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun”. Living joyfully takes application. It is something you have to make happen.

He goes on: “for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.” God made this woman for you. She is the portion you have been given in this life and in all the work you do under the sun, so receive her as the gift she is and live joyfully with her.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 11:8-9
precepts.why:
Adam said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.” Just as Adam had dominion over the creatures he named, he named her. So there is no confusion about why the woman was made, Paul says: “For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man.” “Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man.”

People debate and say we all come from the woman, so how can the man be over her? They do not know the Bible. The woman came from the man. That is thus saith the Lord; argue with God. God created the woman for the man, and nobody can create or remake their own purpose in life.

So many people, men and women, spend their lives fighting against their God-given purpose. It is self-sabotage: you will destroy your whole house trying to be something you are not. And you wonder why you are dealing with spirits of depression and anxiety and always on edge: it is because you are fighting against your God-given role. You cannot change it, and trying only brings confusion.

Out of all the beasts of the field there was nothing fit for the man, so God made him a woman, and that woman has a purpose: help meet for her husband. Sometimes the help starts to think she is the purpose, that she is the house. No: you are the help meet for me and my house. The sooner you accept the truth, the sooner there will be peace in your home and peace within yourself; turmoil comes when you leave that place.

That is where it all went left. Eve knew the rule, but the serpent spoke to what was already within her: “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” She wanted the position that was over her. Paul goes back to the beginning for the same reason: “For Adam was first formed, then Eve.” “And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.” And Sirach says, “Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.” All she had to do was stay in her role and in order.

You might think it too far-fetched that your beloved wife, the mother of your children, the woman who takes care of you, could have the goddamn devil over you while you sleep. But the first woman, the first created by God himself, was susceptible to the devil. You think your wife ain't? That is why the head has to keep reminding them of their place and role in the home.

precepts.label: Genesis 3:16
precepts.why:
“I will make him an help meet for him.” To help is to give assistance or support to someone, to provide something useful or necessary in achieving an end. Meet means suitable for him. So the help is the one who assists in making what the husband wants happen. Sometimes the help thinks she is supposed to lead, or thinks she is supposed to guide, but that is not what a help is.

Genesis 3:16 comes after the transgression: “thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” Some have taken this to mean it was only at this point that the woman was supposed to listen to her husband. No. She was told she was the help back in Genesis 2; Genesis 3:16 confirms the rule after the fall.

So why do we feel today that being a help is a bad thing? Sisters, the help is the greatest thing you are ever going to be. The moment you decide being the help is not the greatest thing you can be, or think you are supposed to be something outside of the help, you are going to destroy your marriage.

It cuts both ways. Brothers, the moment you decide not to provide, not to leave the house and work, not to be the man God told you to be, watch what happens to your household: your marriage will crumble and your life will be in shambles. It is a domino effect. And headship is maintenance, a routine thing a husband has to keep doing. A wife will never say she is trying to overthrow you, but it is in her spirit, the same way a man wants to do things his own way when he gets orders from those ranked above him. So you will have to remind her: I am the head, you have to listen to me.

precepts.label: Isaiah 3:12
precepts.why:
Write this down: women were never designed to lead men. God made the woman “an help meet” for the man, and when that order is turned around, Isaiah 3:12 calls it what it is: “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.”

That is a curse. It is not a good thing; it shows things out of order, not how God set it up. A woman's body alone shows she was not made to lead men into danger: her cycle comes, she is pregnant for nine months, and she is supposed to lead you somewhere?

Women ruling over you is a curse, brothers. Some of you are scared to lead your house and have let her lead. If you are passive, scared, afraid of confrontation, she is going to walk all over you. It is not a secret; everyone sees it, and other men see it in your demeanor. You have to change the way you think. Stand up and take your place back.

The women were designed to be a help to their husbands. When they step outside of that, and when the brothers allow it, chaos follows. That is why there is dysfunction in our nation right now: because the men do not want to lead.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 31:22
precepts.why:
“How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.” A new thing: women being over men was never heard of. It is not natural, and it is not the natural state of a man to be run by a woman. But you allow it.

God did not set it up that way. In Genesis 2 he made the woman a help meet for the man. When she compasses him instead, the order is upside down.

Cases come up where a brother does not know what is going on in his own house. His wife pays all the bills while he is on the couch playing video games, and he cannot understand why his home is in confusion. It is because his wife is running things. She has been the breadwinner from day one, so she looks at it as normal, and he is used to it. He did not want a wife; he wanted a mama.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 34:31
precepts.why:
“And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God, saith the Lord God.” The Lord uses men to lead. It has always been that way and it is never going to change. You will not change the order of things just because you are weak, or scared of your wife.

Sisters, the beta men on social media are influencing you, making you think the man is supposed to worship the ground you walk on. That will not influence the men in purple and gold. We are not worried about being called names, narcissist or misogynist. The question is, do you want a man or do you want a boy?

When your husband gets around the brothers and comes home acting different, he is supposed to. He examines himself, sees he is lacking, and comes home on fire to fix his house, with a little more pep in his step and a little more to say. The same goes when he has been rebuked for adultery or for not dealing with his wife the right way: he is supposed to move different. It works in every area if he truly believes.

This is why there is an attack on the household. Satan and his people know that to destroy us they have to attack our foundation, and the foundation is the home. Paul warned that in the last days perilous times would come, with those “Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof”, and “of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.” They get in through the phone and the conversations, whoever is influencing them. We are building a nation, and if we are not strong on the home front, we will not get off the ground.

precepts.label: Malachi 2:14
precepts.why:
In Eden there was no courtship, no feast and no attraction language. God took the rib and made a woman, “and brought her unto the man.” God formed the union himself, and behind that union is a covenant. Malachi shows it: “the Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth”. God was the one who did the first marriage, and God is in the midst of every marriage; what God joins together, man is not to put asunder.

The world kept pieces of this. When a minister says, before the Lord and all these witnesses I now pronounce you man and wife, that is a rudiment of what the Bible says, and a rudiment is only a part, not the whole.

A covenant is a contract. People understand contracts: a sports fan understands a player's contract, you understand the contract for your job and the contract for your phone plan, but somehow we do not understand the contract of marriage, which is far more powerful and profound. Covenants are built on commitment and obligation, not feelings: if you do this, then this will happen.

God speaks of the wife “against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.” Even if you are being treacherous with your wife, or she with you, you are one flesh, and that is still your companion, the wife of the covenant you made.

Signing a contract on feelings is how people get ripped off buying a car: they like the smell and the color and end up paying the interest rate and the add-ons. Some brothers marry that way: I will deal with all this because she is bad. She is not going to be bad forever. When you get old and the hormones change, you have to be able to live with that person through every dinner, every drive and every wake-up. It has to be stronger than romance and attraction.

Modern ideas about marriage assume feelings are the foundation: find the love of your life, find your prince charming. That is the confusion. The marriage God ordained in Eden stands on his order and on the covenant he witnesses, and that is what carries it through the trials.

precepts.label: Matthew 4:1
precepts.why:
“And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?” Where are you, Adam? I put you down here to rule this earth, and now I'm looking for you. “And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked”. He was afraid because he knew he had messed up. Naked means exposed to sin. They were not running around without clothes; they were never supposed to have the knowledge of sin, and now sin was in them. And Satan showed it to Eve first.

To show what Satan did, the class read how he tempted Christ, from Luke 4. Christ was “led by the Spirit into the wilderness, Being forty days tempted of the devil.” That is what brothers are going to go through: you will be tempted, and a man is supposed to be able to resist temptation. Women are not as strong as men, which is why she is supposed to look up to you. Christ resisted.

First the bread: “If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread.” You have the power, so why sit here hungry? It was an attempt to make Christ forget why he was fasting, the way a cupboard full of food tempts you to forget your purpose. “It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.” Women will forget the course they are on, and that is why men have to protect her. She is in serious trouble without a husband.

Then Satan raised the stakes: “And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” That is what Satan did to Eve. He likely hit her several times while she resisted, and then showed her something greater: you do not have to be under your husband; a time will come when you will be over him. He showed her America, with the man serving her, selling drugs for her, committing crimes for her, worshipping her. She spiritually fornicated with Satan, and brought it back to Adam with her beauty, without telling him about the death, and he took the bait.

When the reckoning came, Adam blamed her: “The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.” It was not her fault; God put him over her, and Adam did not have to listen. Then she blamed the serpent: “The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.” The family unit was attacked. The family is the backbone of the nation, and once husband and wife violate each other's roles they work against each other instead of for each other, and the children come out confused and troubled. That destruction came down through the generations to husbands and wives today. Men must restore the order and bring back our civility.

Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:3
precepts.why:
Respect is taught in childhood, and it starts with “Honour thy father and thy mother.” Leviticus says it the same way: “Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father, and keep my sabbaths: I am the Lord your God.”

The Lord understands the importance of structure, and it has always been there. You are to fear every man his mother and his father, and that goes on into old age. Don't think that once you turn 20 you don't have to listen. That power is always there: you honour your father and your mother.

And wives, once you become someone's wife, you also have your husband to deal with. The same power a father has over his daughter is handed over to her husband when he gives her away, so the respect a child learns for father and mother is the first line of the respect a wife owes her husband. That is how honouring father and mother connects to a wife respecting her husband.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 5:16
precepts.why:
Moses repeats the commandment: “Honour thy father and thy mother, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee; that thy days may be prolonged, and that it may go well with thee, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.”

It was so important for them to honour their father and mother so that their days would be prolonged, so they would not die, and so it would go well with them in the land. The Lord knew from the beginning that the inner structure of the home is what builds the nation.

When there is dysfunction, anything not aligned with how God set it up, there are going to be problems, and it affects the whole nation. Certain households affect other households. If your house is out of order and you are best friends with so-and-so, your kids play together and learn the same bad behaviours. If a sister is a gossiper running from home to home and she is your wife's best friend, it is only a matter of time before your wife is called a gossiper too. Same with you: kick it with the murmurers and you will murmur.

You will infect the nation if your household is not in order. God is about order, always has been. A child raised in a household where the father and mother both understood the laws of God, operated within their roles and demanded obedience to God is more likely to carry that legacy on. Everybody still makes a choice, but the probability follows the household.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:23,25
precepts.why:
Husbands are responsible for provision, leadership, instruction, and showing honour in the household to the wife and the children. Exodus 21:10 shows the provision: “her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish”. He has to provide for his wife's basic needs. “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel”. That is how bad the Lord sees it.

Ephesians 5 describes the husband's role as sacrificial leadership: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body”. And verse 25: “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it”. He gave himself for it. It is a sacrificial relationship.

That is why the brother who destabilizes the whole household economically is out of order. Hard times may come and the wife may hold it down for a while, as in Tobit, where she took woman's work to support the house. But Tobit did not say, you're doing good, so I'm going to play around and figure out what I want to be when I grow up. Brothers here have done that: not happy with the job, so try this business, since the wife makes good money. Knowing damn well you couldn't take those risks by yourself, you take more risk with more lives on the line than when you were responsible only for you.

The husband's measure of accountability is the heavier one. He is the saviour of the body: accountable for his wife, the house, the children, and for those moving for the nation, the nation behind that too. He puts his soul on the line for that accountability, and that is what giving himself for it means.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:7
precepts.why:
“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel”. The knowledge and the honour you give is the commitment to play your role as a husband in all matters. Not, this is the wife you gave me. Not complaining, and not hating her, because the scripture says no man ever hated his own flesh. You deal with the situation.

Men have a moral sense in us, most of us, though some are full of error and lack that integrity. “The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him”. Integrity is doing what's right when nobody's looking, when nobody is there to hold you accountable, like Paul said, not in my presence only. A just man moves with integrity in how he manages and steers his household and in everything else he does as a man of God.

And his children are blessed after him because he raised a stable, sound household. Dwelling with your wife according to knowledge and giving her honour is part of that provision, leadership, instruction and honour the husband owes the house, the same duty Exodus 21:10 says he shall not diminish.

precepts.label: Esther 2:12
precepts.why:
Leviticus 12:4 says “she shall touch no hallowed thing, nor come into the sanctuary, until the days of her purifying be fulfilled.” Purification means being washed, cleansed, made holy; literally, removing what is foreign and contaminated to restore something to its natural clean state. So purification is not just staying away from the temple. The days of her separation are also her being nursed back to health, restored.

Esther shows purification too. Go there and read it for yourselves: Esther went through her days of purification with sweet odours and so forth, and everything else she needed, and she had maids to help her. It is a different purification, but it shows that purifying a woman is a lot of stuff: care, help, the right food, the things her body needs.

So it is with a woman after she gives birth. She was not just sent home and left alone. For those forty days, or eighty for a girl, she was kept in a special place, and midwives and family came, cooked the right food and nursed her back to health. That is postpartum in the Bible, and it is why a sister who has just given birth needs people around her and help with the baby, not the postpartum depression that Esau made up.

precepts.label: Numbers 30:3-5
precepts.why:
Numbers 30:6-8 is about your prayers, sisters, and the power the Most High gave the husband over the wife. If the husband hears her vow and holds his peace, “then her vows shall stand”; but if he disallows her the day he hears it, “he shall make her vow which she vowed, and that which she uttered with her lips, wherewith she bound her soul, of none effect: and the Lord shall forgive her.” Some of you will go to the Most High praying against your husband, and he can say, Lord, do not listen to that trash.

Keep reading back in the chapter and it speaks of the father, for those of you who do not have a husband. It starts with the man: “If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word”.

Then: “If a woman also vow a vow unto the Lord, and bind herself by a bond, being in her father’s house in her youth”. Being where? In her father’s house. “And her father hear her vow, and her bond wherewith she hath bound her soul, and her father shall hold his peace at her: then all her vows shall stand”.

“But if her father disallow her in the day that he heareth; not any of her vows, or of her bonds wherewith she hath bound her soul, shall stand: and the Lord shall forgive her, because her father disallowed her.”

So God also gave the father power over the daughter. The same power the husband has over the wife’s vow, the father has over his daughter’s vow while she is in his house. That is the order the Most High set, and nobody made it up: do not get mad at us, we are reading the Bible.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:1
precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 7:6 says the Lord chose Israel “to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.” Deuteronomy 28:1 says it as well, with the condition attached: “if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth.”

If God says we are above all people and above all nations, then why can we not do the things we have a concrete visual example of other nations doing, and doing for decades? When one of the Amish gets married, the community comes together and builds a house for that couple, and there is no mortgage attached to it. They do not even have power cars. We have enough knowledge, enough builders, plumbers and concrete men; we can do this too, at a higher level.

It is going to take work to build this kingdom: work, and faith that we can do the work, shown by our actions. We need to fix our credit scores, fix our health, learn group economics, and work together in the trades, so that when the tough times come, losing your job because of your last name or because you are tracked, we have things set up to help each other.

This is the highway of the upright, the Israelite's strait journey. Ezra saw that “A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things”, but “The entrance thereof is narrow, and is set in a dangerous place to fall”, with fire on the right hand and deep water on the left, and one path “so small that there could but one man go there at once.” That city is the kingdom of heaven, and we must pass through all these things in this captivity to inherit it.

At the end of it, “the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.” We were ransomed out to the nations, but we are returning and gathering together. Being set on high above all nations is the promise to the people who hearken and do the work.

Deuteronomy 11:12 says the land God gives is “A land which the Lord thy God careth for: the eyes of the Lord thy God are always upon it”. God has his eyes upon a specific place for us. But there is another land his eyes are upon for a different reason.

“Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth”. America is a sinful kingdom, and God is looking at America to destroy it. “saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith the Lord.” Jacob is the father of the twelve tribes of Israel.

“For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.” We were scattered into all nations in slavery and captivity, so he will sift us out of every place we went. The sifting is a teaching process: our people have been trained after the ways of their colonizers, their oppressors and enslavers, and now they must be trained in the word of God to establish the house of Israel.

“All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” Those are our people who are rebellious to what God has to say and want to do things their own way. That is what America, aka Egypt, has convinced you to believe: nothing can happen to you here. You hear Donald Trump saying we have the strongest military, no one can stop us, open the Strait of Hormuz or I will blow you back to kingdom come. Stop believing you cannot be touched because this man talks tough and proud. America's kingdom is temporary; the strength that lasts comes from keeping God's commandments.

precepts.label: Matthew 28:19
precepts.why:
Amos 9:9 says, “I will sift the house of Israel among all nations”. Christians read Matthew 28:19 and think it means make everyone disciples: “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost”.

This is what it means: because we were scattered into all nations, we have to be taught in all nations. It is the same sifting Amos speaks of. Christ himself, when he started his ministry, told the twelve, “Go not into the way of the Gentiles”, but “go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” Teaching all nations is going into all the nations where the lost sheep were scattered.

That is why the bishop gives the order: look historically at where our people were slaves, and go there and train them how to behave for God, to establish the kingdom. They have been trained after the ways of their colonizers, so we must train them in the word of God. The brothers who travel find the hardest thing is telling oppressed people that Jesus Christ is not a white man, because that white Jesus, made up in the Renaissance, is how the colonizers modified their behavior. But the charge stands: tell our people, you are not black, not Hispanic, not West Indian, not African; you are the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

When a man takes a wife and says, “I took this woman, and when I came to her, I found her not a maid”, who is the accusation against? The father. It is his household. He brought his daughter forth saying, this is my daughter, she is a virgin, I have taken care of her, I have watched over her.

That is why Sirach speaks to fathers: “Hast thou children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth. You are their parent, over them, the head of the household, losing sleep watching over your children. A daughter learns order from the household in the beginning, and her father is the first form of respect she has: honouring her father and her mother. Show yourself cheerful and you begin to blur the lines, and once the lines are blurred, so is her perception of authority. So when she gets older, how is she going to deal with her husband?

“Marry thy daughter, and so shalt thou have performed a weighty matter”. It is weighty because the man now has the power you had over your beloved daughter: the little girl you brought into this world, watched after and lost sleep over. Her clothes, her food, her home, where she lays her head: he is in charge now. If I marry my daughter to a crazy negro, I failed; I did not vet him. precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 47:1
precepts.why:
“And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David.” So we know who we are talking about: this is David, in the days of Nathan the prophet, the prophet the Lord sent to him after Bathsheba. The next verse carries on: “As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel.”

That is the same David of 2 Samuel 11. He went out on the roof, “he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.” Bad to the bone. He sent and inquired: I got power, let me send some people over there, let me make this official. One with a spiritual mind made it plain: this is the wife of Uriah the Hittite, this is somebody's wife, bro. “And David sent messengers, and took her” anyway. Wisdom and understanding were right there, and he pushed them aside.

“and she came in unto him, and he lay with her”. She wasn't right either. She didn't resist, she wasn't opposed; she thought she came up. “And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.”

You see how Satan can deceive you. Satan put that lust in him to where he just didn't care, and he went the extra mile: he put Uriah in the front of the battle, got him killed, and took the wife. What he saw, the desire, the action, the cover-up, and the consequences: his first child was gone. Yet Sirach remembers David as the one chosen out of the children of Israel, and that leads to what the Lord did with him.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 47:11
precepts.why:
“The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” The Lord did forgive David. He loved David, and David messed up.

David saw Bathsheba from the roof, took another man's wife, put Uriah in battle to be killed, and lost the child. That is as bad as it gets. But David repented, and the Lord took away his sins, exalted his horn, and gave him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel.

And that's another thing. A lot of times we are going to fall and do things that are not comely according to the scriptures. That don't mean you bunker down, go into a fetal position and say woe is me. You get yourself together, you repent, and you move forward. You don't go back. What did Christ say? Go, and sin no more.

You got to pick up the pieces and keep moving. We are all going to make mistakes. It is how you handle the mistake: it happened, so what are you going to do now, moving forward?

precepts.label: 2 Samuel 14:25
precepts.why:
“But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.” Beauty became part of Absalom's identity. It was synonymous with him: his hair, his physical perfection.

And what came behind that? Ambition and rebellion. You get a big head about yourself and you start to believe certain things. Absalom rose up against his father, it came to civil war, and he died hanging from that very hair, the same thing that was vanity to him.

That is the same lesson as David on the roof in 2 Samuel 11:2. David saw a woman “very beautiful to look upon”, he saw her, he inquired, and he took her, the same pattern as Shechem with Dinah. Out of one fleeting moment of attraction came adultery, the murder of Uriah, a national scandal, the death of the child, and chaos in David's house the rest of his days. The Lord forgave him, but he left him with drama for moving that way. Then Absalom, celebrated for his own beauty, came to pride and rebellion.

Whenever physical attraction becomes the forefront of anything, the Bible shows you that trouble comes behind it. Y'all take chess and spades seriously, seeing moves ahead and counting books, but not marriage: she look good, I got to marry her so I can have her. Attraction is the gateway to destruction if that is the only thing you are moving on.

precepts.label: Proverbs 6:25
precepts.why:
This is why the scripture says these things: “Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” The scripture teaches you not to lust after her beauty, and it says where: in thy heart, in thy mind.

“neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” She gives you the look back. You make the eye contact, you feel the chemistry, the sparks fly, the tentacles of auras come out and they embrace, and you done lost your mind. I got to have her. Bring me that. That's what I want.

That is exactly what happened to David in 2 Samuel 11:2. He walked on the roof, saw a woman washing herself, “and the woman was very beautiful to look upon”, and he moved on what he saw. Shechem saw Dinah and took her, and it ended in violence and massacre. Samson went after the one who pleased him well, and it ended in betrayal and blindness. David saw Bathsheba's beauty, had to have her, and it ended in adultery and murder.

So Solomon's warning is the guard against the very thing David fell into: do not let the beauty get into your heart, and do not let the eyes take you. Attraction is not the foundation, and a man who moves on it alone gives up his strength.

precepts.label: Proverbs 7:10
precepts.why:
“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” There is the physical again: the attire of an harlot and subtil of heart. She is trying to entice, and you fall for it. It works.

Here Solomon warns about being captured by appearance. How does he know these things? He said not one out of a thousand of the women he dealt with. He knew, and he probably knew before the thousandth. It goes to show how intoxicating it can be. You get caught up.

That is the thread through David on the roof in 2 Samuel 11:2. Shechem saw Dinah and took her: violence and massacre. Samson, she pleased him well: betrayal and blindness. David saw Bathsheba's beauty and had to have her: adultery and murder. Absalom, celebrated for his own beauty: pride and rebellion. And the strange women, being beautiful, lead to ruin.

That is why the Bible rarely makes much of the beauty of wives. Rebecca is known for her character, her hospitality and her faith; Zipporah's beauty is never described; Elizabeth is called righteous, not beautiful. What is highlighted in our foremothers is righteousness, obedience, wisdom and faith. The Bible doesn't deny attraction; it just isn't the foundation.

precepts.why:
Eliphaz says to Job, “Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” A lot of brothers go out and teach, some at camp 30 days in a row, 100 days, 365 days. We strengthen the weak hands: people come into the body sick and needing help, marriages come in messed up, and we dedicate our time to figuring out how to fix them.

That is Galatians 6:1: “Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.” Brothers will fall, sisters will fall, people in the congregation will fall, and we spend a lot of our time restoring them, bringing them back up, getting them back in position and making them better than they used to be. We do it for everybody else.

As a leader in this truth your phone rings all day: can I counsel with you, I've got a question. We answer, we deal with it, and when we don't know the answer we go to leadership and get counsel for their counsel. “Thy words have upholden him that was falling”: put the cigarettes down, bro; stop smoking weed; see, the Bible says this.

But the verse says, “considering thyself”. Inside our own household we don't do it. Our wife asks a question and we say, go watch 15 minutes with the captains. We deal with everything on the outside, but we are not teaching and building up our own possession. So when it comes upon us, “thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.” You freeze up, you fold up, and you go against your own counsel, because most men don't counsel about what is going on in their own household. The one who restores everybody else has to consider himself too.

Isaiah shows it: “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness.” The Lord refers to us as trees of righteousness.

In Psalms 1 he refers to us as trees whose leaves are not going to wither, meaning those trees are healthy, those trees are nourished. What kind of tree doesn't bear fruit and its leaves wither? A tree that's unhealthy, and an unhealthy tree is going to wither and fade away. It's the same analogy for us as human beings that God created from the earth. A tree needs water, a tree needs sun, a tree needs nourishment from the earth, the same way we take nourishment from the earth.

precepts.why:
“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.” The law of God is perfect, it is pure, there is nothing wrong with it, and converting means to change. Only the law can change you. I used to be a murderer; the law said thou shalt not murder. I used to be a thief; the law said thou shalt not steal. I used to be an abuser. Once I know the Lord, I repent. Same thing, brother. Same thing, sister, with your trauma. Stop using your trauma as a crutch. It happened when you were 14, 15, 16, and now you're 46, 50, in your third marriage, still using it, and you can't keep a man or a woman because you cannot cope.

We never grew up around order, structure and unity. So when we come around it now, we begin to feel uncomfortable, because we realize we are the problem: the reason environments become toxic, the reason people bicker and fight, the instigating spirit we grew up seeing. Now, in a body and a truth where the light shines on that, you are forced to change, and brothers and sisters do not want to.

“Whoso feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.” If you fear the Lord, you are going to direct your friendships aright, because as you are, so shall your neighbour be. But if you are constantly having issues, constantly having problems, who is the issue? Who is causing these troubles? With the laws of God and all the examples in the scriptures, you should be able to direct your friendship aright. So why is your name always in something?

“My son, gather instruction from thy youth up: so shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age.” We didn't have the opportunity to gather instruction from our youth up. But coming into this truth we have to be born again and begin to do so. You can't drag in all the ways your grandmama and your auntie and them used to deal with each other. It's a new day.

precepts.label: Sirach 6:20-21
precepts.why:
“She is very unpleasant to the unlearned.” Wisdom is very unpleasant to the unlearned. You didn't learn about yourself. All you ever did was point out other people's problems. You never examined yourself; you never looked in the mirror. So now that wisdom finally reveals who you are, it is very unpleasant.

“he that is without understanding will not remain with her.” That's why people have to find a reason to leave. They get offended, they find a reason to be mad, and then they go. What is the root cause? They don't want to change once that wisdom is revealed. And the law, which is perfect, converts only the soul that will be changed.

Destructive attitudes begin internally before they become visible externally. A person may still attend services, teach, lead, pray or serve while harboring the wrong spirit, an evil spirit. You look at the fringes and think, he's good, she's good; you would be surprised how many have an evil spirit in the midst of us. Some come here to destroy the unity of the brotherhood, because in the world it's always chaos: you never see a room full of black people with no fight, no argument, breaking bread together. Whatever you were going through in the world, you had better get over it, and quick, because that thing will destroy you. Those who carry that spirit will find themselves outside these doors.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:47
precepts.why:
“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. The Lord gave us the abundance of all things, and we did not want to serve him for it. So he caused us to serve our enemies, and that is why we ended up falling underneath these people. That is not where our position is supposed to be.

Before we went into captivity we were celebrating the gods of the nations, and the Lord had a problem with that. Psalms 96:5 is his message and warning to us: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.” Our God made everything; that is the God we are connected with. So-called Christmas, Thanksgiving and so-called New Year's are pagan, evil hella days, not holy days. How can you talk about Thanksgiving on stolen land?

We are not the nations. “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” “He hath not dealt so with any nation”. Our customs are his statutes and judgments; we have the Bible, not idols. And Jeremiah 10 says, “Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel”, “Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them.” Astrology, witchcraft and voodoo are the nations' problem, not ours. The Israelites are a special people, set above the nations, the jewels of God, and you have to see yourselves that way.

“For the customs of the people are vain”, void of anything credible: “one cutteth a tree out of the forest”, and “They deck it with silver and with gold”. That was the custom in the Babylonian empire, four empires before Christ was born in the time of Rome. What do lights, tin and silver on a tree have to do with Christ? Nothing. It is Sol Invictus, the unconquered sun, sun worship commemorating Nimrod, Tammuz, whom the women wept for in Ezekiel 8, celebrated on December 25th. Our people know Christ has nothing to do with it, the same way the Bible gives no white Jesus, but they will not stand up for truth.

Serving the gods of the nations instead of serving the Lord with gladness is what put us under our enemies. Anybody who continues to celebrate that madness now knows better and will be judged by the Most High.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 10:12-13
precepts.why:
“Pride goeth before destruction”. Where does pride begin? Sirach: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That means you have a froward mind.

“For pride is the beginning of sin”: the beginning of you falling to sin, falling for your temptation, falling to your lust, falling to feed that appetite. You knew better. You had all the warning signs, all the opportunity, everything placed in front of you. You were given a way out, as 1 Corinthians 10:13 said: God will with the temptation make a way to escape. But pride overcame you. Your mind wasn't on the Lord when your back was against the wall.

“and he that hath it shall pour out abomination”. When you have that pride, a negro is unstoppable; a prideful negro, oh my God. “and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.” When pride overtakes you, the Lord adds things to your demise: I'm going to leave you to Satan to gobble you on up, because your mind ain't right; you're too prideful.

That is why pride goes before destruction. Pride removes correction; you don't want to hear it. You think you know it all, you have all the wisdom and understanding. Pride isolates you, and it precedes the collapse.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 1:3
precepts.why:
Sirach says pride begins when one departs from God. The Wisdom of Solomon shows how a man departs: “For froward thoughts separate from God”.

Being froward means you are thinking outside of the Bible. Period. That's what it is.

When your mind is not on the Lord, you are separated from him. You can't be both. So pride starts in the thoughts: the moment your thinking goes outside of the scriptures, you have separated yourself from God, and a haughty spirit is on its way to the fall. That is why the man who meditates on the scriptures has something to pull from when temptation comes, and the froward man doesn't.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 25:1-2
precepts.why:
This is how much the Lord hates pride. Sirach first shows what God loves: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

The unity of brethren the Lord loves; the love of neighbors the Lord loves. And a man and wife that agree together: why is that beautiful? Because it's hard for two different personalities to come together and be on the same accord. That's why marriage takes time, brothers and sisters. It isn't overnight; it takes years and experience.

Now the negative: “Three sorts of men my soul hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth.” He is offended at their life. A negro that's poor and proud: I hate that negro, I hate his soul, I hate everything about him. How can you be that way?

It means you have no humility whatsoever. Nobody can tell you anything; you have all the answers, but no fruits in your life, no solutions, no shame. That is the pride that goes before destruction, and God's soul hates it.

precepts.label: Psalms 127:1-5
precepts.why:
“The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.” Why are they blessed? Because he raised a stable, sound household. The other purpose of marriage is “Be fruitful, and multiply”: marriage is nation building, and that implies children if you are able. Psalms 127 explains why.

“Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.” The house is the house of marriage, the foundation of it, and by extension Israel as a people. That is why it is so important to handle this right: if you let the world build the house, you are going to get what we have repeatedly gotten as a people.

“It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.” Why put yourself in a situation and then say woe is me, I am miserable in my marriage, full of sorrows, as if you had no control, power or authority, and as if God were not on your side to fix it?

He did not randomly decide to talk about children; he started with building a house. “Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.” That is how we carry on. “As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth.” If the just man walks in his integrity, his children are in good condition.

“Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed.” They are not ashamed because you raised them godly, and it is not only what you tell them but what they see and experience in you as an example. “but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate”: that is the purpose. They follow behind you and fill your shoes, to point out the evils of our oppressors, to point out the evils of our people, and to give them the hope of salvation that they know not.

So the children of the just man are blessed after him because of Psalms 127: the Lord built the house, and the man kept his integrity in it.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 24:12
precepts.why:
“She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.” That is the kind of wife you want, brothers. There was no kindness or wisdom in the email that attacked leadership over the one instance of a leader put out for adultery, while ignoring the three bishops and the seven or eight deacons who were in the midst of no such thing. For every solution we try to give, that spirit has two problems. That is not wife material; they are idolatrous women, some of them idolatrous evil black women, and they will try to destroy your life. Be mindful who you marry.

Now see what language God uses when Israel is in the midst of sin; he uses it in the female context: “She hath wearied herself with lies, and her great scum went not forth out of her”. There is one word that is often wanted but is hurtful to say, so God says it. Your scum is still in your mouth, sisters.

Scum is a layer of foul or unwanted matter that forms on top of a liquid, such as pond scum or soap scum. Informally it means a despised, immoral or worthless person or group, the scum of the earth. The slang meaning goes further: the epitome of a worthless, good-for-nothing human, at the bottom of the hierarchy of humans, possibly the worst word you can have your name associated with. It describes someone so disgraceful they are seen as the lowest form of life: worthlessness, a waste of skin, dirt, nothing. Because it is perfectly acceptable English and not a swear, it is even more demeaning; it is used only when it is the only word for the job, and it makes the victim feel like the lowest of the low.

That is the word God chose for his own people when she wore herself out with lies and the wickedness would not come out of her. Some of these evil sisters are the scum of the earth; that is what God is saying. So examine yourself, and open your mouth with wisdom and the law of kindness instead.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 6:10
precepts.why:
“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. What is the thing? Solomon tells you in chapter 6: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.” The thing is man on earth.

So “that which is done is that which shall be done”: whether man keeps the commandments or does not keep the commandments. “and there is no new thing under the sun.” From the time of Genesis, as it has been is going to be so in these last days. There are no new incidents on this earth; the things done by man are the things that were done in the past. And “There is no remembrance of former things”, because the spirits from the past return to the future.

Paul says the same in different words: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Written for our learning today, because the things done in the past reoccur. In a Christian mind everything is new; but nothing is new. To deal with these reoccurring events, we must read the history and testimonies of our ancestors.

Ezra shows it too: “I will liken my judgment unto a ring”. A ring is a circle, “like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” It is a continual event that reoccurs over and over. And the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets”, comparing one thing to another.

That is why what we read in Daniel 3, Nebuchadnezzar setting up his golden image, is coming to pass again with the Trump administration and the golden statue the pastors prayed over. The man that hath been is the man that shall be.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 26:23
precepts.why:
“Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun”. Brothers, who gave her to you? The Lord did. Look at your wife: that sister was created for you. “for that is thy portion in this life”.

Now some of you are saying, God did that? She all jacked up, though. Here is another surprise: “A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man: but a godly woman is given to him that feareth the Lord.” Nobody here wrote the Bible. That is what the scripture says.

So ask yourself, why is she jacked up? Because you're jacked up; she was created just for you. Brothers see all of her flaws, all of her issues, every problem she has, and look at themselves like they never did anything wrong. Ask yourself: why was she given to me? What am I doing, what am I not reflecting on, how am I not being real with myself, to understand why I am in the situation I am in?

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 26:3
precepts.why:
“A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear the Lord.” A good wife is given to him that deserves a good wife: to them that fear the Lord. She is the portion Solomon spoke of in Ecclesiastes 9:9.

So think about this, brothers. If you are not serious about this walk in this truth, not serious about what you are supposed to be doing, how could you expect a righteous woman? Everybody says, I want that virtuous woman. But you nasty. You have been committing adultery since you have been in the truth, and you want the Proverbs 31? No, sir. You get the scum, the bottom of the barrel. Why? Because of where your faith is at.

Now, let's be real: it is not always the case. Sisters will say, well, if I messed up, that means you messed up. No. Sometimes a husband is trying to get you right. Sometimes he is trying to correct you, trying to show you what he wants so that you can be who he wants you to be. It ain't always him.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 7:26
precepts.why:
Here is the reality check for the evil sisters who think, well, if I'm evil, he's evil, we're just going to be evil together. Solomon says: “And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her”.

Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her. A man will be delivered from that type of woman. He will escape; he will get away.

So, sisters, don't think you can just be evil and die that way and the two of you will be together forever. No. The Lord will deliver him. How about we just repent and get our stuff together, so you can be heirs together? The wife the Lord gave is meant to be lived with joyfully all the days of your life, as a portion, not as a snare.

precepts.label: Romans 8:19
precepts.why:
“Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” Man was put on this earth to rule it with God's commandments, and because we are not doing that, the earth is suffering; we are not in power. The earth was made to receive your direction, men.

Paul shows it: “For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” Expectation means I am expecting something, and earnestly means with a begging type of attitude. The creation is earnestly waiting for the manifestation, and manifestation means the growth: time for us to stop being kids and manifest into men, to get ourselves together. The earth is waiting for the sons of God to manifest into gods, that is, to rule this planet properly.

And righteous women are waiting for that too. The woman is called woman because she is of man, and she is like the earth: you plant your seed in her and she brings forth fruit, but she needs your guidance. She is supposed to revolve around you, and when you are not in rulership she is out of orbit, like a satellite floating in space with no direction. That is why women cry, where are our black men? The father figure in the house got destroyed.

All of it fell apart when we broke the laws of the Most High from the very beginning, when the woman was out of order with her husband. So it is up to us men to fulfil the duty of manhood to fix it: to marry, build a nation, and rule rightly. That is what the whole creation is waiting on.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:14
precepts.why:
Verse 13 gives the whole duty of man; verse 14 gives the reason: “For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” For means because. Keep his commandments, because this is the whole reason God put man on the earth, and because God shall bring every work into judgment.

So if we are not dealing with our marriages properly, there is going to be a judgment for that, and we are looking at it. People try to figure out the problem in the black community: the marriages are messed up. Whoring, adultery, fornication. A little leaven will destroy the whole congregation, and it has to be rooted out like a cancer.

“with every secret thing”: the nasty stuff people do behind closed doors, thinking nobody sees. In nearly 35 years in this truth, we have seen the Most High bring out what people thought they could hide, and he brings it out at the worst time for you. Like applying for a job years later, thinking you got away with it, and they pull records you didn't know existed: get out of my office. That's how the Lord is.

So keep your slate clean. Be a disciplined man: you may not always be motivated, but you must always be disciplined. When sin comes before you, it stops right there. Because every work, good or evil, is going to come out, we have to be men of holiness, integrity, righteousness, dignity, honor and valor. That is the whole duty of man.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 10:20
precepts.why:
God shall bring every secret thing into judgment, and the Lord even calls a bird to bring it out: “Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.” We have sat in judgments where they asked, how did he find out? It's that damn bird. Somebody might think it's a literal bird flying around; I took every precaution. But the Most High is going to bring it out anyway. That's why it says every secret thing.

No, not in thy thought. Some people speak against the council and the leadership, or have evil thoughts against the leaders, and think they will get away with it. The Most High put leadership to watch over you, and that is not an easy job. Leaders must give an account, good or bad. The goal is to give a good account: the brother came in one way and now he is a man of valor, married, moving in the right direction; the sister listened to counsel and got herself together. When they will not take counsel, the leader still has to give an account, with grief.

This is how we should have grown up. We grew up in a lawless society; in slavery the fathers were stripped from the homes and the men forced to give their seed but not allowed to raise it. The matter will be told on you in your evil, so fear God, keep his commandments, and honor the ones set over you.

We look for it to come from somewhere outside. We externalize everything instead of taking up what is already in us. The Lord put a mind and a spirit in us to build and to organize.

You were made after the image of your Father, and Genesis shows how he created. “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. And the earth was without form and void”. “And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.” God imagined what light should be. “And God saw the light, that it was good”: when he created it, he compared it to the image in his mind, and it was good, meaning it conformed to his thoughts. He did the same with the earth: when it was all done he said it is good, because it matched the earth he had in mind before it was even created.

Because we are made in his image, we have the ability to do the same thing: to organize and put things together in our minds before they become physical. That is what Christ is saying: “Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.” Everything you lay your eyes on, apart from the ground, the vegetation and the water, came from a thought. People cannot believe that IUIC can envision its buildings before bringing them into existence, but we are supposed to think like our Father. precepts.why:
The disciples asked, “Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind?” They were asking about something Christ had taught them, the regeneration. He answered that in this case it was neither, “but that the works of God should be made manifest in him”.

But paying for the sins of the fathers is real, and Matthew 23 shows how it works. Christ tells the scribes and Pharisees, “ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity”. They “build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets”. They were saying, that wasn't us.

Those who led us into captivity on the slave ships have not yet gone into captivity, but they are going, because they have to fill up the measure of their fathers. The iniquity of the fathers was the murder of the prophets, and it was visited upon the children, the Pharisees of Christ's day. Those born in the third and fourth generation pay for the sins committed three or four generations ago.

The Most High caused him to be born blind so that he could be healed later, and the Lord may allow a situation anywhere so he can exercise his mercy and his power on it as an example to the rest of us. Then why are there so many problems in Israel, so much confusion about the husband's position and the wife's position? Because pride has made its way in, and confusion has set itself in the house.

“and the head of Christ is God”. Was Christ ever confused, at any moment in his life, about his position and role with the Father? He said: “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

Christ said, I am doing exactly as the Father told me to do. Is he doing what he wants? No. Christ understands his role and his position. And Christ now tells us the husband is the head of the wife. So why is there still so much confusion? Somebody does not believe like they say they do.

It happens on both sides of the room. Brother, because of your lack of leadership, because you are non-confrontational and passive and don't want no smoke, she raises her voice and you cower; she walks by shoulder-bumping you, and you can't raise your voice in your own house. All because you gave up your position. Some brothers want to be mama's boys: you didn't want a wife, you wanted a mom. If Christ submits to the head over him, the husband must take his place under Christ, and the wife her place under her husband.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:23
precepts.why:
“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” Paul is not making anything up. He is not creating a list and saying, I'll place this person here and that person there. He went to the divine order that was set forth from the beginning, when Adam named his wife Eve, and he does it in other places too.

Ephesians says it again: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church”. Is there any confusion there, brothers? The husband is the head of the wife, just like Christ is the head of the church.

So the order runs: the Most High God, Christ, the husband, and the wife. If anybody tries to step out of their role or out of their position, what are they? The damn devil. That goes for the men too: men who step out of their role and want to be a mama's boy, you are the damn devil. You have been given a position; you must fill it.

There cannot be a commandment you are negotiating on. All of us struggle with something, and we know the fight, but never be the one who says, I can get with everything else but that right there I just can't do; he's an idiot, I can't follow him. That is not what the scripture said.

precepts.label: Colossians 1:18
precepts.why:
“the head of every man is Christ”. Colossians shows it: “And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead”. Christ is the head of the church.

And Christ himself is under a head: “the head of Christ is God.” Christ said, “The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do”. And, “the Father loveth the Son, and sheweth him all things that himself doeth”. How could the Father show the Son if the Son was the Father? If you are still stuck on the Trinity, go sit in the corner. It makes no sense for the Most High to show his Son something if they are the same entity.

“For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son”. Here we see order being given, and the headship of the household falls under the same order. “That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father.” To honour the Son is to honour what he said; if you do not honour the order God has given you, you are not honouring the Lord.

Christ said, “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” He is letting us know that he himself is in the divine order and submits to the position he has been given. What do we look like doing anything other than what Christ did?

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 11:2
precepts.why:
“For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband”. The espousal was made when the Most High sent his son Christ, because Christ died for us, his woman. We are the woman of the Most High. We are men physically, but we are his bride, and that is why Paul uses that term.

He cleaned us up. Sanctified them through thy truth; thy word is truth. Once he cleaned us up, we became virgins with him: “that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” That is crystal clear. It is what 2 Corinthians 5:17 means: “if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away”.

There is such a thing as history, but your history only comes up if you keep doing what you used to do. Then it becomes a blot on your record today. None of us was born in this truth, so whatever you sisters went through, and the same with you brothers, clean yourselves up while you are here. All of us have a chance to get ourselves correct.

Once the slate is cleaned, we do not dirty it up. We do not defile it or mess it up. That is how we stay a chaste virgin espoused to Christ.

precepts.label: Revelation 14:4
precepts.why:
“These are they which were not defiled with women; for they are virgins.” That does not necessarily mean they are virgins physically. They are virgins in this truth. They put off the weak nature, the sins and the cares of the world. They are the ones that came in and repented, the new creature of 2 Corinthians 5:17, where old things are passed away and all things are become new.

“These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. These were redeemed from among men”: redeemed from among the filth. To be redeemed means you were in the filth, in the vomit, at a serious deficit, and you had to be brought up out of it. We were redeemed from that, “being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb.” We have been cleaned up for the Lord, men and women, so we have a chance and an opportunity to get it right.

“And in their mouth was found no guile”: no lies, “for they are without fault before the throne of God.” How can that be? Only when you are keeping the commandments of God and the faith of Christ.

So watch how you move. Replay your own actions in your mind, see how you are operating, and catch yourself, because there is an effort to take us off our path. The virgins who follow the Lamb keep the slate clean.

thread.text: Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you,

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:5
precepts.why:
“Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you”. When the brothers teach on the street, that is what they tell our brothers and sisters: come out of the sinful lives you are living in, out of Babylon the great, out of these wicked holidays like Christmas. But if we tell them to come out of something, they have to come into something. They have to have something to say yes to, like righteously enjoying the commandments of the Lord through the high holy days. An organized nation thinks on all of these points and deals with the nation holistically.

They lose their wicked parents and wicked friends when they come in, so the Lord says “I will receive you”, and “will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters”. Your fathers out there did not teach you anything. Your mothers did not teach you anything. So the Lord gives you fathers and mothers in this truth.

That is why Peter says “Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder.” When our brothers and sisters come in, they are going to have to submit to the leadership, to the elders who now stand as their fathers and mothers.

When you are received, you are not abandoned or left out in the cold. You were lost, but now you are found: welcome home. Now we have belonging, now we are loved, wrapped in the Most High's care, and that makes you stand up with esteem and refuse to let mediocrity deter you from the righteous path.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 5:2
precepts.why:
“The elder women as mothers”. The mothers out there did not teach anything. The daughters ran wild, the sons ran wild, and the daddies taught nothing. But the children heard the prophets say, come out of that. So the elder women in this truth become mothers to the sisters who come in without proper guidance. That is the importance of you elders, and why we thank the Lord for the sisters still holding on to righteousness, because Satan went after our sisters and got a lot of them messed up.

“the younger as sisters”: the younger women become sisters to the disenfranchised sisters coming in. A sister who comes in does not know how to put a skirt on, dress properly, carry herself or hold a righteous conversation. She learns from sisters who were guided by proper mothers and fathers in the body. The brothers are the same: we are a proper influence on brothers who came from total dysfunction. And it is to be done “with all purity.”

Sometimes the children get fixed up first and go back home to that sinful family. The parents notice the righteous change and ask the reason of the hope that is in them: where did you learn this respect for me, when I have been nothing but a bad father or mother to you? Then those parents come in and become repentant mothers and fathers.

This is how the Lord keeps his word, “I will receive you”, and “will be a Father unto you”. The whole nation, men and women, elder mothers and elder brothers, becomes the family we all need, and when you marry, you carry it on to your children through your generations.

precepts.label: James 1:14
precepts.why:
Paul fears “lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted”. Satan is able to see what is within you, and that is what he attacks: not the stuff you are strong in, but the stuff you are weak in. “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” The temptation comes from something already within you.

So if you have a problem with wanting to be the head honcho, wanting to be over your husband, wanting to be the shot caller in control of how things go in the home, Satan plays with that, and you will look up and there will be a complete role reversal in your home. Subtle means pleasing to the senses in a mild or nuanced way. That little bit of power feels good: I decide what we eat around here, I put up the curtains, I picked this out. Then you start overstepping your bounds and do not even know it was Satan who set you up with the curtains. Sisters, when you start to overstep your divine place and purpose, say, that's Satan, you almost got me.

Most of us have been infected by the westernized mindset: birthdays, baby showers, Mother's Day and Father's Day, Thanksgiving, the ring on the finger, rules God did not make that we think are how life is supposed to be. The same goes for how a man deals with his wife. A father who told his son, get your money, the hoes are going to come, and left a condom on his dresser for him, normalized it. That residue has to be let go completely, or it will cloud your judgment and ruin your marriage.

It is the house of the man. Joshua said, as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord; he did not say, in agreement with my wife. He commanded his home. And some brothers take themselves out of that role and want to be a mama's boy in the marriage, wanting her to mother them instead of leading her. That emboldens her, and now you are her child and that is how she speaks to you. Both are drawn away by their own lust, and Satan works subtly on what is already within.

precepts.label: Romans 13:14
precepts.why:
“Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” What does it mean to walk in the Spirit? It does not mean moonwalking or walking on the air. Romans explains it: “But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ”, that is, the commandments and your faith, “and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.” To make provision for the flesh is not walking in the Spirit.

To make provision is to make a way for you to fulfil that lust, leaving doors open for the sin. Why are you on the phone with your ex? You are going to end up banging her. If you are struggling, delete Instagram and delete certain things; put controls on your phone so you cannot go on certain things. People say, I made a mistake, I slipped and fell, I don't know what happened. So you were walking and just slipped and fell on the dude? There was planning. You were talking to him first, and you planned what day to meet up. It was already in your mind. It was a decision, not a mistake.

With porn, if it is that bad, get rid of social media. Do not say, I can handle it, I'm good. That is Satan telling you that, and leaving it open keeps fuelling the lust, because every time you go on you see a bunch of different stuff. Some of you say you repented but leave little doors open, and you fall back into that sin. Sit down and talk to yourself: I am dealing with this, so I need to set things up so I do not fall into it.

Because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”. It is a war: you want to stop, you stop for a week or two, and it comes back. The works of the flesh are “Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness”, all sexual sins. That discipline applies in marriage too: forty or eighty days after your wife gives birth, and her seven days. Satan does not come when you are dealing with your woman; he comes when you are not getting any. Those are the days to fast more and occupy yourself with the Lord. As men we cannot let pleasure control us.

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
“he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.” When you sow yourself into the scriptures, the Lord is going to give you blessings: he will show you favor, have mercy on you, and give you abundance. That is Joshua 1:8: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.”

We should meditate on the scriptures day and night, “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.” Meditating and doing is the sowing.

When we do that, the Lord makes our way prosperous. He gives us the abundance we desire, spiritually, emotionally, all the increases we desire, when we put our mind on the Lord. That is reaping of the Spirit.

precepts.label: Romans 6:23
precepts.why:
“whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.” What you put in, you are going to reap. When you put in the sin, the consequences are going to happen, period. Paul says it plainly: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Sin is death. That is the corruption reaped by the one who sows to his flesh: sow that sin to your flesh and you will be judged by it. And the gift of God, eternal life through Christ, is the “life everlasting” reaped by the one who sows to the Spirit.

What you put in, you are going to receive as a reward. Wages for sin, a gift for the one who sows to the Spirit. God is not mocked.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 30:19
precepts.why:
The Lord set both harvests before Israel from the beginning: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.”

What you put in, you are going to get; you are going to receive a reward. Life and blessing for the one who sows to the Spirit, death and cursing for the one who sows to his flesh. Heaven and earth are called as witnesses, so no one can say he was not told. God is not mocked.

And the choice reaches past you: choose life “that both thou and thy seed may live.” What a man sows, his children reap with him.

precepts.label: Joshua 24:15
precepts.why:
“And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve.” You cannot serve two masters. You can't serve the flesh and serve God at the same time. You have to choose; ain't no in between.

That is why he said he would rather you be cold or hot. If you are lukewarm, battling that middle ground and playing games, he will spew you out of his mouth. Sowing to the flesh and sowing to the Spirit cannot be done at once.

“whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.” Choose the Lord, sow to the Spirit, and of the Spirit reap life everlasting.
